newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's railway to build $233 mln double track.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's railway to build $233 mln double track.

text.p: Morocco's state-owned railway said on Wednesday it would invest 2.167 billion dirhams ($233 million) to build a 136 km (85 miles) double track.
"This investment will ease traffic on this railway," an official at the Office National des Chemins de Fer said.
He said the project would be carried out by the Moroccan-Spanish consortium SGTM, SCC Bimatec and Obras Guinavard.
The segment, linking Kenitra, 40 km (25 miles) from Rabat to the central city of Meknes, will be financed by loans from the World Bank, the European Investment Bank and the Arab Development Bank.
The double track, expected to be operating by 2002, will raise passenger traffic to 80 trains per day from the current 61 and goods trains to 34 from 26.
